test_title: PYST 1: SSC CGL Tier - II (Quant) (Held On: 8 Aug 2022)
subject: maths
question: Two trains whose lengths are 450 metres and 300 metres are moving towards each other at the speed of 162 km/hr and 108 km/hr respectively. If distance between trains is 300 metres, then in how much time, these trains will cross each other ?
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Relative Speed = (162 + 108) × 5/18 = 270 × 5/18 = 75 m/s.

Total distance to cross = Length 1 + Length 2 + Gap = 450 + 300 + 300 = 1050 m.

Time = Total Distance ÷ Relative Speed = 1050 ÷ 75 = 14 seconds.

**∴ The correct answer is 14 seconds.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of first train (L₁) = 450 m

Length of second train (L₂) = 300 m

Distance between them (D) = 300 m

Speed of first train (S₁) = 162 km/hr

Speed of second train (S₂) = 108 km/hr

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7dc2dfe9b01065e84653a5a0fcf7ab4af5191a3759662aeb4e0722a5b64ace05.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Relative Speed (Opposite Direction) = S₁ + S₂

⇒ Relative Speed = 162 + 108 = 270 km/hr

⇒ Conversion to m/s = 270 × (5/18)

⇒ Relative Speed = 15 × 5 = 75 m/s

⇒ Total Distance to cover for crossing = L₁ + L₂ + D

⇒ Total Distance = 450 + 300 + 300 = 1050 m

⇒ Time taken = Total Distance ÷ Relative Speed

⇒ Time taken = 1050 ÷ 75

⇒ Time taken = 14 seconds

**∴ The correct answer is 14 seconds.**

**__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed in Opposite Direction

When two objects move towards each other, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds: Vᵣₑₗ = V₁ + V₂.

Unit Conversion (km/hr to m/s)

To convert speed from km/hr to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert from m/s to km/hr, multiply by 18/5.

Total Distance for Crossing

To cross each other completely, the trains must cover the initial distance between them plus the sum of their own lengths.</p
